body:
incident-bot: PAGER: Elevated 429s detected for org=acme-corp across hosted inference-prod (region: us-west1). Error rate > 20% for last 3m. Severity: high. Paging oncall: @emily (oncall)

emily: seeing it. graphs look spiky on token-insert throttle metric. Acme traffic surged ~3x due to a backfill job.

emily: quick assessment — 429s are coming from per-org rate limiter. Their configured rps cap is 1000 req/min (~16.6 rps). Backfill is causing bursts and the limiter pile-ups cause queuing and 429s.

samir: tagging in — I can take over if you want, emily. About to step away for feed.

emily: plz take, throwing a temporary hotfix now. leave note for handoff.

emily: proposed mitigation options: 1) bump org limit for acme-corp temporarily; 2) apply burst allowance window; 3) disable streaming for that org to reduce connection pressure; 4) throttle downstream model selection to smaller variants. Prefer (1) + (3) for fastest effect.

samir: agreed. will run admin hotfix: increase per-org rate limit to 3000 req/min and disable streaming for acme-corp. also add a short-lived quota ticket.

maria: heads up — disabling streaming may change response shape for their integration. CS should warn them.

cs-team: on it. drafting message to Acme support lead: "we're applying a temporary mitigation to reduce 429s; will share timeline and rollback plan".

samir: executing CLI command now:
```
# internal admin CLI
redwood-admin org update --org acme-corp --set rate_limit=3000 --set streaming=false --meta emergency_hotfix=true
```

ops-bot: RUNNING: redwood-admin job 8273 started by samir (dry-run=false)

ops-bot: SUCCESS: job 8273 completed in 6s. New org settings: rate_limit=3000 req/min, streaming=false, meta.emergency_hotfix=true

samir: monitoring... immediate drop in 429s on the per-org rate-limiter metric. overall 429 rate for acme down from 22% -> 2% in 90s.

ryan: checking for side effects — any queue growth on model-serving? KV-cache look stable. No increase in N+1 errors. latency unchanged.

maria: thanks. CS, please ping the customer note now and offer to reverse if they see functional regressions.

cs-team: message sent to acme-support@acme.com and slack:acme-eng. Snippet: "We're applying a temporary emergency hotfix (increased request cap, disabled streaming) to mitigate 429 errors observed across your workload. Expect normal responses but streaming may be impacted. We'll follow up with timeline and re-enable streaming after traffic normalizes."

emily: great. can we add a global guard to prevent similar single-org spikes from starving others? We should also consider auto-burst policy per SKU.

samir: opened quick task: HOTFIX-291 add short-term org burst allowance config + rate-limit circuit-breaker. Not shipping here, just tracking.

ops-bot: ALERT: overall cluster token throughput increased 45% after hotfix. Capacity headroom still >= 12% in us-west1. No immediate capacity alerts.

samir: note: I also added a temporary attribution tag so we can roll back the change easily: meta.emergency_hotfix_by=samir, meta.hotfix_expires=1710514050 (4 hours).

emily: handoff to samir completed. I'm stepping out. Samir, you'll lead the mitigation/resume.

samir: acknowledged. monitoring alarms set: alert if latency > 800ms or 429 > 5% for 5m.

(20m passes)

samir: update — traffic normalized, 429 stable at 0.8%. CS reported one customer-reported missing chunk due to streaming off; they accepted a temporary workaround and asked for reenable ASAP.

maria: we should re-enable streaming under a controlled rollout. Plan: re-enable streaming for acme at 10% of connections, monitor 429s for 10m, then 50%, then 100%.

samir: will do a gradual reenable via admin API with rollout param. Running:
```
redwood-admin org update --org acme-corp --set streaming=true --rollout=10% --meta rollout_stage=canary
```

ops-bot: RUNNING: job 8289 (streaming canary) started by samir

ops-bot: SUCCESS: job 8289 completed. Canary at 10%.

samir: monitoring canary: no 429 spikes after 15m. proceeding to 50%.

ops-bot: RUNNING: job 8290 update streaming to 50%

ops-bot: SUCCESS: job 8290 completed.

samir: 50% -> stable. moving to 100%

ops-bot: RUNNING: job 8291 update streaming to 100%

ops-bot: SUCCESS: job 8291 completed. streaming reenabled fully.

samir: rolling back hotfix meta and resetting rate limit to previous 1000 req/min.

samir: running rollback command:
```
redwood-admin org update --org acme-corp --set rate_limit=1000 --set streaming=true --unset meta.emergency_hotfix --unset meta.hotfix_expires
```

ops-bot: SUCCESS: rollback job 8292 completed. org config restored.

samir: final check: 429s remain low, latency normal. No residual alerts. Closing active mitigation.

emily: thanks for the handoff and clean rollback. Please add an incident task list for postmortem and preventative work (auto-burst policy, better telemetry on org backfills, notify-before-backfill opt-in).

samir: created PM ticket: PM-742 "Acme backfill caused org-rate-limit hotspots" with action items: (1) auto-burst policy prototype, (2) per-org backfill detection + preemptive notifications, (3) improve oncall runbook for hotfix commands + safe rollback.

maria: I'll own the canary rollout tooling improvement (reduce manual steps).

cs-team: CS will follow up with Acme and offer a one-time quota increase and post-incident summary.

ryan: adding monitoring improvements: add metric for "org burst factor" and an alert when single-org token share > 35% for 5m.

emily: closing notes: severity lowered to resolved. Marking this thread for postmortem. Good ops. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: severity -> resolved. Duration: ~45m. Root cause: uncoordinated backfill from acme-corp causing burst beyond per-org limiter design. Mitigation: emergency temp rate bump + streaming disable, graduated reenable and rollback. Actions: PM-742, HOTFIX-291, monitoring alerts.

(End of thread)
